thread:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Paging: SLO breach (streaming tail stalls) - severity: P1. Notified on-call team.
Ana: saw alerts — p95 jumped from ~240ms to ~2.4s, p99 ~12s for streaming/chunk responses in us-east-1. Some clients reporting timeouts and reconnect storms.
Michael: I'm on it. Initial hypothesis: proxy layer buffering is holding chunks and then timing out, causing client backpressure.
Devon: logs show a lot of repeated 'upstream write timeout after 45s' from streaming-proxy. Example: `ERROR streaming-proxy: upstream write timeout id=req-4f2a3b cn=client-78`
Sophie: customers: 2 enterprise customers reporting partial streaming failures on checkout flows (payments). CS pinged them.
Priya: Concurrency pattern: sudden spike in long-lived streams after model rollout 03:00 UTC. Could be a change in model latency distribution (longer tails).
Ana: stack traces show proxy accumulating per-connection buffers; memory per worker approaching config limit. Need to reduce buffering.
OpsBot: Suggestion: toggle streaming_proxy.chunk_buffer_ms -> 50 (currently 4000) for lower latency.
Michael: Preparing a safe change. Plan A: reduce chunk_buffer_ms on streaming-proxy configmap and restart one worker at a time. Plan B (if rolling restart risky): route traffic for the two impacted customers to bypass-proxy path (bypass-preserve-kv) and route to fallback model variant.
Devon: Rolling restart command ready: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/streaming-proxy -n infra --field-selector spec.template.metadata.annotations.restart=now` — doing canary on node pool-a first.
Sophie: Customer Success: we're telling customers "we're mitigating, will update within 15m", asked for workarounds — sending the retry guidance.
Ana: Quick mitigation enacted: increased proxy keepalive and reduced chunk buffer to 200ms on a single canary pod (applied at 3920012348).
Michael: Canary looks promising: that pod started serving clients with p95 down to ~420ms, p99 1.8s for its subset. However other pods still show heavy buffering.
Devon: Observed side effect: some clients expect larger chunk windows — reducing buffer leads to more frequent small chunks; one legacy client misinterprets chunk boundary and retried. Noted.
Priya: Telemetry: request rate for streaming endpoints up 32%, average tokens per stream up 18%. Might be correlated.
Ana: Action items (short term):
- finish canary rollout of reduced chunk_buffer_ms to 50ms across streaming-proxy (controlled, one zone at a time).
- enable route fallback for two impacted customers to model redwood-small-1 (lower tail latency).
- enable temporary prefix KV caching for frequent prompts.
Michael: Executing route update: `redwoodctl routes update --customer=acct-893 --route=checkout --fallback-model=redwood-small-1 --traffic=100%` (applied at 3920012355).
OpsBot: Confirmed route change propagated to edge in 2 zones.
Sophie: CS: customers on fallback reported progress, one sees partial restores for streaming checkout (still some dropped bytes).
Devon: Observability: trace sample for failing request: `trace_id=tr-7a9c, events: proxy_write->client_pause->proxy_retry->upstream_reset`. Suspect client-side backpressure + proxy queue compaction bug.
Ana: Running live dump on one of the failing proxy workers: `sudo journalctl -u streaming-proxy -n 500 | grep "holdback"` shows repeated 'chunk holdback exceeded 30s, flushing' which aligns to client disconnects.
Michael: Opened a short-lived rollback of the recent model rollout (rolled back model-tag 2026-03-12) for one cluster to isolate model vs infra.
Priya: Rollback took effect at 3920012368, p99 dropped from 12s to ~3.2s cluster-wide in ~2m. That strongly points to model-induced longer tails interacting with proxy buffer policy.
Sophie: CS: informing customers of rollback and mitigation steps; asking them to re-test.
Ana: Next steps (medium term):
- update streaming-proxy to respect Client-Send-Window and more aggressive chunk flush for long-inflight requests.
- add circuit-breaker to avoid single long stream flooding buffers — cap per-client in-flight bytes.
- add an automatic fallback policy when p99 > 5s to route to smaller model variant.
Devon: For now, I've scheduled a hotfix patch to streaming-proxy's chunking algorithm (change holdback eviction threshold from 30s -> 5s) — patch built, need canary deployment.
Michael: Can we set a temporary global SLO mitigation note? Ops: mark the incident as SLO-impacting, set status page message.
IncidentBot: Incident status updated -> Investigating -> SLO breach noted. Status page draft: "We are investigating increased tail latency for streaming responses in US-East impacting a subset of customers; mitigations in progress."
Priya: Monitoring: create alert to trigger if p99 > 5s for 5m sustained across any region.
Ana: Hand-off: Oncall Rotation @maria will take over in 20m. I'll document actions taken and outstanding.
Michael: Outstanding: verify no data loss, assess retry storms. Devon/Infra to review proxy memory growth timeline.
Sophie: CS: logged all impacted customers, two enterprise customers still affected but on fallback; internal ticket created CS-4592.
Customer Success: please escalate any active customer calls to the emergency line, we have engineers on the bridge.
Devon: Patch canary started at 3920012380 on zone-b; logs show chunk eviction now firing earlier and partial reduction in buffer memory.
Ana: After patch canary: p95 ~300ms, p99 ~1.4s on canary; cluster-wide still converging.
Michael: I'll keep the on-call loop updated. If the patch holds for 15m across both zones, we'll promote and close short-term mitigation.
Oncall Rotation: taking over. Thanks team — I'll continue follow-ups and prepare full incident writeup after stabilization.
Sophie: :thumbsup: Good job.
IncidentBot: Incident severity downgraded to P2 at 3920012390 — ongoing mitigation, customer impact reduced.
